Jordan — quick assessment after a first pass with finance: Sentinel is strategically high-priority (healthcare vertical, potential reference). Economics look OK if we lock at current unit rates for 3 years but we need guardrails. My recommendation: approve a 3-year price lock with a 7% annual uplift cap (instead of 5%) subject to the following conditions:

- Minimum annual commitment of 18M ARR floor (to be measured quarterly)
- Allow a bilateral material change clause: if our underlying delivery costs increase >12% YoY (validated by published cloud/GPU cost indices), we can reopen uplift discussions (cap to be negotiated, not to exceed 12%)
- Renewal protection: no unilateral above-cap increases during the term; post-term auto-renewals limited to 12-month terms and any increases must be <= uplift cap and communicated 45 days prior
- Customer may pause auto-renewal on a per-product basis but only if they give 60 days notice and maintain minimum spend floor at account level

If execs approve, we should add a one-time margin protection reserve (retention credit structure) rather than ongoing discounts. I can prepare a redline for legal to review tonight.

Marissa
Director, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Sentinel_redlines_v1.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: 3yr price lock + uplift cap and renewal protection

Team — legal review (high level): Marissa's conditions are workable but we need to tighten language around the "material change" trigger and the metrics used to validate cost shifts. Proposed edits:

- Define the cost index (public cloud instance price index + NVIDIA spot pricing blended index) and set a 12% threshold measured on a trailing 12-month window
- Cap the maximum uplift in renegotiation scenarios to 12% in any 12-month period
- For renewal protection, replace "pause auto-renewal" with an explicit "opt-out" process: customer must deliver written notice 60 days prior to renewal and provide evidence of consumption decline; Redwood reserves the right to require a mitigant (short-term buy-down or one-time credit)
- Require exec approval for any concession that increases expected discounting by >25% vs. standard list pricing over the term (this will include the proposed 7% cap + commit floor trade)

Please confirm if we should present the above as our opening position to Sentinel or escalate directly to execs for an exception. If exec review is required, Ben and Naomi should be looped for sign-off.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec approval request: Sentinel Health — 3yr lock + uplift cap (decision required)

Naomi — requesting exec sign-off for an exception on terms for Sentinel Health (DEAL-2028-0117). Summary of proposed package: 

- 3-year price lock at current unit rates
- 7% annual uplift cap (holding the customer's requested 5% as aspirational but not feasible without lower economics)
- Minimum annual ARR floor: 18M; measured quarterly
- Renewal protection: no above-cap unilateral increases during the term; post-term auto-renewals limited to 12 months with 45 days notice for price changes
- Per-product opt-out available with 60 days notice but account-level minimum spends still apply

Rationale: high strategic value (referenceable), predictable committed revenue, and strong expansion potential. Tradeoffs: some margin compression in years 2-3 if consumption ramps less than forecast. Finance projects a mid-single-digit IRR impact but acceptable given reference value.

Asks: 1) Exec approval to offer the package above; 2) Authority to finalize legal redline consistent with Karthik's edits; 3) Permission to sign a 3yr SOW pending counterparty acceptance.

If approved, I'll instruct Deal Desk to submit the formal offer and legal to prepare the final SOW for procurement.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
